passage:
Prof. Divyansh: Binita, please sit. This paragraph reads very differently from your earlier work. Did you use an AI tool?
Binita: (heart pounding) ...Yes. Partly.
Prof. Divyansh: Which part?
Binita: The summary section, and I asked it to polish my sentences. The analysis is mine. I have my handwritten notes and the first draft here.
Prof. Divyansh: Thank you for saying so directly. Show me the notes.
Binita: (sliding over the pages) I didn't read the course rules properly. I thought polishing was fine.
Prof. Divyansh: The rule asks you to declare any use. Let's read it together, then we can decide what to do with this submission.
Binita: Okay. I should have asked first.

qa.q: Which parts did Binita say came from the AI tool?
qa.a: Binita said the summary section and the sentence polishing came from the tool, while the analysis was Binita's own.

qa.q: How did Binita feel when the professor asked about the AI tool, and how can you tell?
qa.a: Exposed and nervous: Binita's heart was pounding before the answer, which came after a pause.

qa.q: What did Binita do that kept a small matter small?
qa.a: Binita told the truth, showed handwritten notes and the first draft, and agreed to learn the rules, instead of lying.

qa.q: How might Prof. Divyansh see Binita's honesty?
qa.a: Prof. Divyansh thanked Binita for saying it directly, so honesty and visible process make it easier to treat this as a rule to learn than as cheating.

grounding: A professor suspects an AI-written assignment when it was partly so, and Binita admits it honestly, shows process and learns the rules.
